```{python}
import polars as pl
```

```{python}
ames = fetch_openml(name="house_prices", as_frame=True, parser='auto')

df = pl.from_pandas(ames.frame)
```

## QUESTION

1. __Take time to get to know your data.__ Based on some initial exploration, identify 3 variables in the dataset you think will have strong predictive ability for determining if a house was built before 1980. Explain/justify the reasoning behind your guesses (for example with plots).

I just looked at the data frame and saw what columns existed. I looked at a few houses, really just skimming the data, seeing if I immediately saw anything worth chasing. 
One that caughe my eye was the garage year built, as older homes were likely to have older garages.
Another was remodeling year, as older houses likely had older dates of remodeling.
And the last I picked was overall quality, as I assume that newer houses tend to have better overall quality than older houses.


```{python}
# Literally just displayed the data and looked at what columns existed
df.head()

# Then created a plot, and tried out a few different variables, and found the ones that had a somewhat coherent relationship with the frequency of the value and year built
plot = (
  ggplot(
    df, mapping=aes(x="YearBuilt", y = "GarageYrBlt"))
  + geom_point()
)

plot
```

2. __Build a classification model labeling houses as being built “before 1980” or “during or after 1980”.__ Your goal is to reach or exceed 90% accuracy. Report your final model choice and any other model parameters you may have tweaked (train-test split ratio, tuning parameters, etc).  

I used a decision tree classifier for my final model. I used a 60/40 train/test split because I tested a couple of split variables and I found that 60/40 gave the best accuracy. I also set the max depth to 5 and minimum samples per leaf to 10, as I found that moving them from what we used in class either didnt change the result or made it worse. In the end, I got 96.92% accuracy with my model.

AI Use: Spent about an hour troubleshooting before asking AI to help solve a couple of errors- Originally I was trying to use columns with text, and I couldn't figure out how to switch them to a format the model could understand, so I ended up using the columns I have currently- I also had a few syntax errors like accidental double periods that it helped me catch.

```{python}
# Creates a target column for the model which is 1 if built before 1980 and 0 if built during or after
df_model = df.with_columns(
  (pl.col('YearBuilt') < 1980).alias('Before1980')
)

# Selects features and targets
feature_cols = ['YearRemodAdd', 'GarageYrBlt', 'OverallQual']
target_col = 'Before1980'

# Selects data for the model
X = df_model.select(feature_cols)
y = df_model.select(target_col).to_series()

# Splitting data into training and testing sets
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y,
    test_size=0.40,
    random_state=42
)

# PRinting results of split
print(f"Total Records: {df.height}")
print(f"Training set: {X_train.height} rows")
print(f"Testing set: {X_test.height} rows")

#  Creating baseline model to compare against
baseline = DummyClassifier(strategy="most_frequent")
baseline.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Calculate accuracy of baseling model
base_acc = metrics.accuracy_score(y_test, baseline.predict(X_test))
print(f"Baseline Accuracy: {base_acc:.2%}")

# Create decision tree model
clf = DecisionTreeClassifier(
  max_depth=5, 
  min_samples_leaf=10,
  random_state=42
)

# Fits data to model
clf.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Predicts values
y_pred = clf.predict(X_test)

# Calculates and prints accuracy
model_acc = metrics.accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
print(f"Model Accuracy: {model_acc:.2%}")
```
